svg.aria-label: Computation flow of one frame: 42 numbered operations from the input image to the depth map, each with the tensors it reads and writes and the memory they live in; parallel work shown with fork and join bars.
svg.text: One frame of Depth-Anything V2 on the board: every computation, in order
Shapes are [rows × columns] of the matrix the operation sees; int16 activations, int8 weights, int32 sums, f32 = 32-bit float. 82 tokens = 81 patches + 1 class token; 384 = the model width.
runs on the accelerator (inside every such job: read engine ∥ 64 multipliers ∥ write engine, see 3)
fork / join: independent work, executed one after another today (could be parallel)
resize photo to 126×126, ImageNet-normalise, quantise to int16 (dav2_image.py)
W image [126×126×3] int16 + one f32 scale, 95 kB, over JTAG
W cols [81 × 588] int16 (81 patches, 588 = 14·14·3 values each)
patch-embedding GEMM: acc = W · colsᵀ — one accelerator job per 64-row tile (2 tiles: 64 + 17 rows)
R cols [81 × 588] int16, 64 rows per tile → tile RAM
R patch_embed.w [384 × 588] int8, streamed once per tile
W acc [384 × 81] int32 and stats [2 tiles × 384 × {max,min}] int32
up to 8 word requests in flight; reord
the three run concurrently; the block is bound by the bus (3.2 cycles per word)
R patch_embed scale [384] f32, bias [384] f32
W params [384 × {mult, shift, bias}] int32; one output scale (f32) for the tensor
requantisation job: emb[n][m] = sat14((acc[m][n]·mult + 2^(s−1)) >> s + bias)
R acc [384 × 81] int32 (read transposed into tile RAM)
the same job follows every GEMM below; written as “+ requant” from here on
tokens: x = [cls + pos₀ ; emb + pos₁..₈₁] (in float, requantised once)
W x [82 × 384] int16 — the token matrix every block updates
Transformer encoder — steps 7–21 repeat for blocks b = 1 … 12 (weights of block b from the blob)
LayerNorm 1: n = (x − mean_row) / std_row · γ + β
qkv GEMM + requant: qkv = n · Wqkvᵀ
W qkv [82 × 1152] int16 = [q | k | v], each 384 wide = 6 heads × 64
6 attention heads: independent of each other — run one after another today
head h = 1 … 6 (columns h·64 … h·64+63 of q, k, v)
gather this head, scale to 11 bits, split the int16 operands into int8 halves
R q, k, v slices of qkv [82 × 64] each
W q_hi = q>>4, q_lo = q&15 [82 × 64] int8 each
W vᵀ_hi = v>>6, vᵀ_lo = v&63 [64 × 84] int8 each (transposed, padded to 84)
softmax per query row: S = 16·S_hi + S_lo; P[t][m] = 2^((S[t][m] −
W P [82 × 84] int16 (Q15, padded), sum[82] int32, 1/sum[82] int64
W ctx head slice [82 × 64], assembled then copied out
W ctx [82 × 384] int16, columns of head h
Why the halves: the accelerator multiplies
int16 × int8. q and v are int16, so each is
split into a high and a low int8 part and the
Per head the accelerator does 4 jobs of
projection GEMM + requant: attn = ctx · Wprojᵀ
residual: x = x + attn (both rescaled to a common scale, saturated to 14 bits)
MLP up GEMM + requant: hdn = n2 · Wfc1ᵀ
GELU in place: hdn = gelu(hdn) (257-entry table, linear interpolation)
MLP down GEMM + requant: h2 = hdn · Wfc2ᵀ
feature tap — only after blocks 3, 6, 9 and 12: feats[i] = LN(x; γ, β)[1..81] (class
R norm γ, β [384] f32 (the final norm)
W feats[i] [81 × 384] int16, i = 0..3 (a 9 × 9 grid of 384-vectors)
DPT decoder — four feature levels, then fused coarse to fine
the four levels are independent of one another — computed one after another today
1536, partial sums added on the CPU)
Result of 22–25: four 64-channel feature maps at 36×36, 18×18, 9×9 and 5×5 — the same content at four resolutions.
Every 3×3 convolution above is: the CPU gathers each pixel’s 3×3 neighbourhood into one row (im2col), the accelerator multiplies, the accelerator requantises.
Fusion — coarse to fine; each step needs the previous one (strictly sequential)
RCU(t) = t + conv3×3(relu(conv3×3(relu(t)))) — two 3×3 convolutions (im2col + GEMM + requant, weights rf·.u·c1/c2 [64 × 576]) with ReLUs on the CPU, plus the input.
path3 = conv1×1( up_9→18( RCU( path4 + RCU(rn3) ) ) )
add on the CPU; bilinear 9 → 18 on the CPU
path2 = conv1×1( up_18→36( RCU( path3 + RCU(rn2) ) ) )
path1 = conv1×1( up_36→72( RCU( path2 + RCU(rn1) ) ) )
3×3 conv, 32 → 32: im2col (CPU, 15 876 rows) + GEMM + requant, then ReLU (CPU)
to float: depth = d · scale; raise the done flag
read the depth map over JTAG (0.7 s), save .npy, compare with the host build (bit-exact), render
Totals per frame: 2 275 accelerator jobs (GEMM and requantisation), 25 MB of weights read from DDR3 twice (once per tile), 15 MB peak of arena in use, 14.2 s at 50 MHz.
